title: Forward the caller's promise parameter to callees
motivation: towers passed its own promise parameters on to its recursive call as new stub promises `[<sym from_peg>]{ deopt 0 [] }`. Each call allocated three promises that nobody forced, and storage had the same pattern. The allocation and tracking of these promises dominated the cost of each call.
solution: `StrictifyPromise` replaces a single-use argument promise by the version's own promise parameter `x`. The promise must be a stub of the symbol that names `x`, or `{ v = force x; return v }`. `x` must be a definite promise whose type matches the callee's parameter, and the callee must not reflect on that parameter or be `@readsPromise`. Other R code must also not see the promise's expression: `exposesFrame` rejects a builtin that runs R code, and a callee version that creates a closure or calls a dynamic callee, a context reader or a GNU-R base closure. For a stub, `bindingHoldsParameter` checks that every `st` of the name stores `x`, that the version has at most one non-regular frame, and that it has no non-static closure or reflective store of the name. `Cleanup` then removes the unused promise.
